concepts.title: Mean of a Data Set
concepts.definition: The mean is the plain average of a numeric attribute: add all the values and divide by how many there are; it summarises a whole column of a table in one number but gets distorted by outliers.
concepts.key_idea: The nine student heights [90, 102, 110, 115, 85, 90, 100, 110, 110] give a mean of about 101.33 cm.
question_patterns: Compute the mean height of the class from the nine given height values.
Why should extreme values be removed before trusting a mean?
The weights of 40 students are recorded. Describe how to state the average weight in one sentence.
A data set holds 6 values whose total is 54. What is the mean?
When is the mean an unsuitable measure of central tendency?

solution_steps.explain: Add every height in the list.

worked_examples.q: Five plants measure 90, 102, 110, 115 and 85 cm. What is their mean height in cm?

concepts.title: Median Position in Sorted Values
concepts.definition: The median is the central value once the data are sorted; with an odd count of n values it sits at position n plus 1 over 2, and with an even count it is the average of the two middle values.
concepts.key_idea: Sorting [90, 102, 110, 115, 85, 90, 100, 110, 110] puts 102 exactly in the fifth of nine positions.
question_patterns: Find the median of the sorted height list [85, 90, 90, 100, 102, 110, 110, 110, 115].
Which position does the median occupy when the data hold 9 values, and what when they hold 10?
Why must the data be sorted before the median is read?
The sorted marks of 8 students end with 62 and 70 in the middle. Compute the median.
How does the median split a data set into two equal parts?

solution_steps.explain: For an odd count the median occupies slot n plus 1 over 2.
One less than the slot number gives how many values sit below the median.

worked_examples.q: Sort 90, 102, 110, 115 and 85. Which value sits exactly in the middle?

concepts.title: Range between Extremes
concepts.definition: The range measures spread using only the two extreme values: the largest minus the smallest, so a single outlier can inflate it; the midpoint of that span is called the midrange.
concepts.key_idea: Heights from 85 cm to 115 cm span a range of 30 cm centred on the midrange 100 cm.
question_patterns: Find the range of the height data whose smallest value is 85 cm and largest is 115 cm.
Why does one outlier badly distort the range?
For which kind of data can a range be computed at all?
Compute the midrange of a data set spanning 85 to 115.
The week's temperatures run from 27 to 34 degrees Celsius. What is the range?

solution_steps.explain: Largest minus smallest gives the coverage.
Adding half the spread to the smallest locates the midrange.

worked_examples.q: Heights span 85 cm to 115 cm. What is the range in cm?

concepts.title: Standard Deviation of the Data
concepts.definition: Standard deviation measures how widely values stray from the mean: subtract the mean from each value, square the differences, average them, and take the positive square root; a small value means tightly packed data.
concepts.key_idea: The nine heights give squared deviations totalling 938, so the variance is about 104.22 and the standard deviation about 10.21 cm.
question_patterns: Compute the standard deviation of the nine height values whose squared deviations total 938.
What does a larger standard deviation tell about a data set?
Why does standard deviation use every value while range uses only two?
The squared deviations of a data set total 938 over 9 values. Find the variance and then the standard deviation.
Which two data sets can share a mean yet differ in standard deviation?

solution_steps.explain: Divide the total of squared differences by the count.
The square root of the variance is the standard deviation.

worked_examples.q: What is the midrange of heights spanning 85 cm to 115 cm?

concepts.title: Mode as Highest Frequency
concepts.definition: The mode is the value occurring most often in the data; a set where every value appears once has no mode, and several values tying at the top frequency make the data multi-modal.
concepts.key_idea: In the height data, 110 appears three times, more than any other value, so 110 is the mode.
question_patterns: Find the mode of the height data [90, 102, 110, 115, 85, 90, 100, 110, 110].
When does a data set have no mode, and when can it have more than one?
Can the mode be computed for non-numeric data such as car colours? Explain.
Which value is the dominant one in the temperatures 34, 34, 27, 28, 27, 34, 34?
A survey of car owners must find the most popular colour. Which measure applies?

solution_steps.explain: Count how often every distinct value occurs; the value with the largest tally is the mode, and a tie shares the title.

worked_examples.q: Which measure of central tendency names the value occurring most often?

concepts.title: Structured and Unstructured Data
concepts.definition: Structured data fits a fixed rows-and-columns layout where each column is an attribute and each row an observation, like the kitchen inventory table; unstructured data, such as newspaper pages, emails or videos, follows no fixed record format.
concepts.formula: rows x columns with named attributes -> structured
concepts.key_idea: Summing the Items_in_Inventory column works only because the data are structured.
question_patterns: Differentiate structured from unstructured data with one example of each.
Classify: a video file, a fee deposit record, a social media post, an ATM withdrawal log.
Which attributes would you maintain for books at a shop?
How can a shop owner use the structured inventory table to find the total value of stock?
Why does an email count as unstructured data?

solution_steps.explain: Data with fixed named attributes per row are structured; free-form text, media or mixed content without a schema is unstructured.

worked_examples.q: Data in fixed rows and columns with named attributes is called what?

concepts.title: Metadata: Data about Data
concepts.definition: Metadata describes other data rather than carrying the content itself: an email's subject, recipient and attachment list, or an image's size, format and resolution, all help programs organise the underlying data.
concepts.formula: metadata = subject, size, type, resolution of the content
concepts.key_idea: A photo taken on a phone carries metadata such as image size, JPEG or PNG type and resolution.
question_patterns: What is metadata? Give the metadata of an email message.
Which metadata would describe an image file stored on a phone?
Does a photograph clicked on a mobile camera carry metadata? Justify.
Why is metadata useful for handling unstructured data?
List the parts into which the metadata of an email divides the message.

solution_steps.explain: Metadata never holds the main content; it records facts such as size, type, author or timestamp that describe and locate the content.

worked_examples.q: An email's subject, recipient and attachment list describe other data. What is such data called?

concepts.title: Data Processing Cycle
concepts.definition: Raw data becomes decisions through a cycle: collect the data, prepare and enter it, store it on devices such as HDD, SSD or pen drive, process it, and publish the output as reports, tables or charts.
concepts.formula: collection -> preparation -> entry -> storage -> processing -> output
concepts.key_idea: An ATM withdrawal shows the cycle at work: PIN and amount enter, the system verifies and debits, and a printed slip comes out.
question_patterns: Draw and explain the steps of the data processing cycle.
Which data must a bank maintain to process ATM withdrawals, and what output does it produce?
List the data needed to issue a train ticket and describe the processing involved.
Why is storing processed data still necessary after the output is produced?
What limitations of plain file processing does a database management system remove?

solution_steps.action: follow one input to its output
solution_steps.explain: Trace the chosen scenario through collection, preparation, entry, storage, processing and the final information product.

worked_examples.q: Which cycle turns raw data into decisions, beginning with collection?

worked_examples.title: Mean height of the class
worked_examples.problem: Heights of nine students in centimetres are 90, 102, 110, 115, 85, 90, 100, 110 and 110. Compute the mean height.

steps.explain: The mean spreads the total over the nine students.

worked_examples.answer_note: The total is 912 cm, giving a mean height of about 101.33 cm.

worked_examples.title: Range and midrange of heights
worked_examples.problem: For the same height data, the smallest value is 85 cm and the largest is 115 cm. Compute the range and the midrange.

steps.explain: Add half the spread to the smallest value.

worked_examples.answer_note: The range is 30 cm and the midrange sits at 100 cm.

For the week's temperatures 34, 34, 27, 28, 27, 34, 34, name and apply the technique for: the average, the spread, and the variation around the average.
